samples.summary: Gate 1b is unrequested scope beyond the task's stated plan and Non-Goal, and it changes promotion behavior for a whole class of PRs. The task file docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md states the Non-Goal "No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior or its exit-code numbering. … only the consumer and the tests change", and its "Scope added after review" list enumerates exactly four additions (path identity, newest-wins invariant, trigger-side path guards, the promote `outcome`) — none of which is gate 1b. The diff nevertheless adds a brand-new promotion gate (`CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES` / `branchEditsCiDefinition` / `ranBaseCiDefinition`) that refuses auto-promotion for any PR touching `.github/workflows/**` or `.github/actions/**`, and fails closed on an unreadable file list. The cost is outside tidiness: every harness PR (including this one) now permanently requires a human to flip it to ready, and the loop reports `gates-unsatisfied` on PRs that previously promoted. If that is intended, the todo's plan/Non-Goals must record the decision; as filed, the spec and the code disagree.
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs adds gate "CI ran main's definition (branch edits no .github/workflows|actions/**)" to the `gates` array; todo Non-goals line 79: "No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior or its exit-code numbering."

samples.summary: The `trigger-shape` canary ships as an inert `.patch` blob under docs/tasks/active/ — precisely the shape this same branch's lessons file forbids. docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-lessons.md:23 records as a lesson: "**A blocked half does not ship as a `.patch` file** … the blob is pinned to blob hashes and line offsets of a 2400-line file other work edits, nothing verifies it, and the task tooling cannot see it … A change that cannot land whole should land as the part that is complete on its own, with the blocked part left in the issue." scripts/agent/rounds.test.mjs:188-193 preserves the same complaint as a recorded major panel finding from PR #564. The todo (lines 102-112) even narrates that the previous `.patch` workaround was deleted by a maintainer because it "is not a landable shape". Reintroducing one — for a canary the issue never asked for — repeats the anti-pattern and leaves harness-engineering.md describing a safety net that does not exist in the pipeline.
samples.evidence: New file docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-trigger-shape.patch containing an agent-review-panel.yml job plus its checks.test.mjs pin; lessons file line 23.

samples.summary: The design doc now contradicts itself about the same gate. The new "Gate 1b: WHICH file ran is not WHAT was in it" paragraph (line 1905) states that mark-ready refuses to promote any branch touching `.github/workflows/**` or `.github/actions/**`, closing the merge-ref hole. Fifty lines later, the retained "**What gate 1 does NOT prove.**" paragraph (line 1960) restates the identical hole as still open and says "closing that needs the run's workflow content compared against the base branch" — with no mention of 1b. A reader of the canonical subsystem doc cannot tell which is current, and the stale paragraph invites someone to re-implement or to delete gate 1b as unnecessary. The `@ref`-tolerance warning is also duplicated verbatim across the 1b and gate-1 paragraphs.
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:1905-1925 (gate 1b closes it) vs 1960-1967 ("Gate 1 therefore means … not 'main's CI definition passed'; closing that needs the run's workflow content compared against the base branch").

samples.summary: The design doc backtick-cites the staged patch file (`docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-trigger-shape.patch`), while the patch's own header instructs "Delete this file in the same commit that applies it." harness-engineering.md is a TOP-LEVEL docs/design file, where the enforced doc-staleness lane requires every backticked path to resolve on disk — so following the patch's instructions reds CI until this doc line is edited too. The doc should describe the canary's status without a path reference that is designed to be deleted (or the canary should simply land with the rest of the change).
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:1945-1948 "It is STAGED, NOT LANDED — `docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-trigger-shape.patch`"; patch header line: "Delete this file in the same commit that applies it."

samples.summary: The new file breaks docs/tasks' documented naming/layout convention. docs/tasks/README.md specifies only `YYYYMMDD-<slug>-todo.md` and `YYYYMMDD-<slug>-lessons.md` under `docs/tasks/active/`, regenerated by `pnpm tasks:index`; a `.patch` artifact is invisible to that index and to `pnpm tasks:archive`, so it will linger after the task is archived.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described (mark-ready.mjs:175-210, gate string at :238) and the quoted Non-goal line exists (todo:79), but the finding's blocking premise — that the decision is unrecorded, so "the spec and the code disagree" — is false. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16,60-65 makes docs/design/ the canonical record for behavior/architecture decisions (task files are execution plans). docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1893-1925 folds gate 1b into the canonical harness doc: it states the exact rule (refuse promotion for .github/workflows/** or .github/actions/**, renames on both names, unreadable list fails closed), why it exists (an agent:managed human PR shares the promote path and is not bound by the App's push restriction), and explicitly accepts the very cost the reviewer prices as harm — "Such a PR is not blocked, only un-automated — a human reviews the workflow change and flips it to ready, which is where that decision belongs." The behavior is also documented in the script header (mark-ready.mjs:16-29) and pinned by tests (mark-ready.test.mjs:262-284). So it is not scope past a Non-Goal the repo decided against; the repo's canonical doc decides for it, and the todo itself already records (lines 47-53) that the "no change to mark-ready.mjs behavior" Non-goal was consciously superseded by review-driven gate-1 hardening. What actually remains is a stale Non-goals bullet plus an un-enumerated scope item (and a leftover contradicting paragraph at harness-engineering.md:1960-1967) — a divergence from the documented plan that still behaves as specified, whose cost stays inside the codebase. Under this lens's rubric that is minor, and minor never blocks; no #937 acceptance criterion is unmet and no duplication exists.
